definition: A bright, open lift — something good is here and you feel lighter for it.
examples: a friend's good news landing well
the first day of a holiday
laughing until your face hurts

definition: A heavy, inward ache — something matters, and it hurts.
examples: missing someone who isn't there
a hope that didn't land
the quiet after a goodbye

definition: A hot, pushing energy — something feels wrong or unfair.
examples: being talked over
a rule that only hurts you
watching someone get treated badly

definition: A braced, alert tension — something might go wrong.
examples: a message you don't want to open
the moment before a jump
a noise downstairs at night

definition: A quiet, steady ease — nothing is pulling at you.
examples: a slow breath with nowhere to be
a room that feels safe
the hush after rain

definition: A quiet, settled ease — nothing missing, nothing chasing you. Not excitement; the soft hum of being okay where you are.
examples: a slow morning with nowhere to be
the first sip of something warm
sitting with a friend in comfortable silence

definition: A bright, bubbly lift — something small and lovely catches you off guard and lights you up.
examples: a dog greeting you like you've been gone for years
finding money in a winter coat
a song you love coming on unexpectedly

definition: A warm turning-toward — being glad that something or someone is in your life.
examples: a friend checking in at exactly the right moment
noticing someone remembered something small you said
a quiet thank-you that really lands

definition: A light, ticklish energy — silly, curious, up for almost anything.
examples: an inside joke that keeps going all day
making up voices for your pet
a plan with no purpose besides fun

definition: A gentle leaning toward what's ahead — not certain, but open.
examples: a reply that says let's talk
the first warm day of the year
applying for something you actually want

definition: A gentle ache for something gone or not yet here — bittersweet, tender, a little faraway.
examples: an old song that takes you back
passing a place you used to go
a happy memory that feels bittersweet now

definition: A heavy sadness after a loss — when something that mattered is gone and the world feels changed by it.
examples: a chair that stays empty
a tradition that no longer happens
not being able to tell someone your news

definition: A soft, lingering sadness with no single cause — reflective, a little grey, not unpleasant.
examples: a rainy afternoon where you stay in
the last light before dark
a film that leaves you quiet

definition: A quiet ache of being apart — missing company, or missing being seen.
examples: a full room where you feel like a spectator
eating dinner with only your phone nearby
a weekend that nobody asked about

definition: A sharp, surface-level friction — small things catching on you.
examples: a sound that won't stop
being interrupted for the third time
a tag that scratches your neck

definition: A hot, surging anger — something feels deeply unfair.
examples: watching someone be treated badly
finding out you were lied to
a decision made behind your back

definition: A slow-burning anger at a wrong that still stings.
examples: always being the one who adjusts
a thank-you that never came
watching someone else get away with it

definition: A restless worry about what might happen — body braced, mind circling.
examples: checking your phone before it buzzes
a message that says we need to talk
lying awake rehearsing tomorrow

definition: A quiet sense that something is off — not danger yet, just unsettled.
examples: a room that goes quiet when you walk in
a familiar place that looks different
a gut feeling you can't explain

definition: A heavy anticipation of something bad — the feeling before the fall.
examples: a meeting on the calendar you can't avoid
the moment before opening bad news
counting down to something difficult

definition: A wide, unhurried calm — nothing pulling at you.
examples: a quiet walk with no destination
the hour after everyone else falls asleep
waking up before your alarm, rested

definition: A steady, rooted presence — you know where you are.
examples: feet on the floor, slow breath
finishing something hard and staying with it
a conversation where you felt fully there

definition: The body letting go after a strain — the long breath after holding it.
examples: hearing the test went fine
the moment a deadline passes
finding the thing you thought you lost

definition: Too much at once — more than your hands can hold.
examples: three deadlines on the same day
a room that gets louder
too many people needing you

definition: A body that won't settle — always reaching for the next thing.
examples: checking your phone every minute
pacing without noticing
lying down but not relaxing

definition: Apart in a way that feels permanent — like the bridge is gone.
examples: the group chat that moved on without you
a weekend with no calls
being far from everyone you know

definition: Present but not noticed — like background.
examples: being introduced and immediately forgotten
a message that never gets a reply
sitting in a room where no one asks

definition: A hurry with no room — waiting feels like friction.
examples: a queue that won't move
waiting for a reply you need now
a slow app on a fast day

definition: A deep, unbothered calm — clear water.
examples: a long exhale after a hard week
sitting somewhere quiet and green
nothing left on your list
